title: Common fixed endomorphisms commute with principal localization and affine sheaves
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a finite set, and $\sigma_i:R\to R$ ring endomorphisms for $i\in I$. No action laws or invertibility of the endomorphisms are assumed. Put $A=\{r\in R:\sigma_i(r)=r\text{ for all }i\in I\}$, a subring, and let $p:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be induced by inclusion [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every $f\in A$, the canonical map $A_f\to R_f$ is injective and identifies $A_f$ with the common fixed subring of the induced endomorphisms $(\sigma_i)_f$ of $R_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. For any open $T\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, each $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma_i$ preserves $p^{-1}T$, so it induces an endomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(p^{-1}T)$. The assignment $\mathcal F(T)=\{s\in\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(p^{-1}T):\sigma_i^*s=s\text{ for all }i\in I\}$, with inherited restrictions, is a sheaf of rings [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. The canonical structure map induces an isomorphism of sheaves $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\cong\mathcal F$, whose component on $D_A(f)$ is precisely the localization map onto the common fixed subring of $R_f$. These identifications commute with restrictions between all opens. No reducedness or nonzero-divisor assumption on $R$ or $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write $j:A\hookrightarrow R$. Since $\sigma_i j=j$, functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ gives $p\circ s_i=p$ for $s_i=\operatorname{Spec}\sigma_i$. Hence $s_i^{-1}(p^{-1}T)=p^{-1}T$ for every open $T$. The sheaf component of $s_i$ therefore gives a ring endomorphism of sections on $p^{-1}T$, natural in $T$. Also $\sigma_i(f)=f$, so the formula $(\sigma_i)_f(r/f^n)=\sigma_i(r)/f^n$ respects the fraction equivalence relation and defines a ring endomorphism of $R_f$.

source.place: algebra-lemma-spec-functorial; schemes Section Affine schemes; agent-written application of functoriality and the fraction definition (00CO)

proof.text: The inclusion induces $j_f:A_f\to R_f$, $a/f^n\mapsto a/f^n$. If its value is zero, the fraction criterion gives $f^ka=0$ in $R$ for some $k\geq0$. Both $f$ and $a$ lie in $A$, and inclusion is injective, so the same equality holds in $A$ and $a/f^n=0$ in $A_f$. Thus $j_f$ is injective. Every fraction in its image is fixed, because its numerator and denominator are fixed.

source.place: Tag 00CO, algebra-definition-localization; agent-written kernel and fixed-fraction calculation

proof.text: Conversely, let $r/f^n\in R_f$ be fixed by every $(\sigma_i)_f$. Multiplication by the unit $f^n$ shows $(\sigma_i(r)-r)/1=0$. Thus for each $i$ there is $k_i\geq0$ with $f^{k_i}(\sigma_i(r)-r)=0$. Choose $N=\max(\{0\}\cup\{k_i:i\in I\})$, using finiteness of $I$. Then $\sigma_i(f^Nr)=f^N\sigma_i(r)=f^Nr$ for every $i$, so $a=f^Nr\in A$. The fraction $a/f^{n+N}\in A_f$ maps to $r/f^n$. This proves the claimed image equality without cancelling any element in $R$. For $I=\varnothing$, take $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 00CO, algebra-definition-localization; agent-written finite common-exponent argument generalizing the original field-quotient Step 4

proof.text: Restrictions preserve the fixed sections by naturality in Step 1. For an open cover $T=\bigcup_\alpha T_\alpha$, compatible sections of $\mathcal F(T_\alpha)$ glue uniquely in $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(p^{-1}T)$, since the $p^{-1}T_\alpha$ cover $p^{-1}T$. For each $i$, the glued section and its pullback by $s_i$ have identical restrictions to that cover, hence are equal by sheaf uniqueness. Thus the glued section belongs to $\mathcal F(T)$; the inherited operations make $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of rings. Functoriality of ringed-space composition and $p\circ s_i=p$ give $s_i^*p^\sharp=p^\sharp$. Corestricting $p^\sharp$ therefore gives a morphism $\theta:\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\to\mathcal F$ compatible with every restriction.

source.place: definition-ringed-space (0091), morphisms and composition; agent-written verification of the sheaf gluing axiom for common fixed sections

proof.text: For $f\in A$, contraction of primes along $j$ gives $p^{-1}D_A(f)=D_R(f)$. The affine section-localization lemma identifies the section rings on these two opens with $A_f$ and $R_f$, using the canonical restriction maps from $A$ and $R$. Under these identifications, $p^\sharp$ sends $a/1$ to $j(a)/1$ and sends the inverse of $f/1$ to its inverse; every fraction is a product of these elements, so its map is exactly $j_f$. The same argument for $\sigma_i$ identifies $s_i^*$ on $D_R(f)$ with $(\sigma_i)_f$. Consequently $\mathcal F(D_A(f))$ is the common fixed subring of $R_f$, and Steps 2--3 say exactly that $\theta_{D_A(f)}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (1),(3),(5), and Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; canonical affine-section maps followed by the explicit generator calculation

proof.text: The opens $D_A(f)$ form a basis by the spectrum basic-open lemma. Apply part (b) of the sheaf-morphism-on-basis lemma to the sheaves $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ and $\mathcal F$ and the morphism $\theta$: Step 5 verifies its isomorphism hypothesis on every basis member. Hence $\theta$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings. Its components and their inverses commute with restrictions on all opens by naturality (compose the naturality square with the component inverses). This is the canonical isomorphism asserted, with the specified principal-open components.
